cards.text: This is Philip, a follower of Jesus. One day an angel of the Lord comes to him with orders: get up and go south.

cards.question: The angel of the Lord tells Philip to go south. Which road does the angel send him to?

answers.text: The desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza
The coast road from Joppa to Caesarea
The hill road from Jericho to Bethel

cards.text: So Philip starts out. On the way he meets an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians.

cards.question: This Ethiopian court official is in charge of Queen Candace's entire ___.

cards.text: Friend, somebody bought ME for a quarter. This man runs the ENTIRE treasury of a queen, and he's just been to Jerusalem.

cards.question: The Ethiopian official had traveled all the way to Jerusalem. What for?

cards.text: Now he's headed home, sitting in his chariot, reading Isaiah the prophet. Then the Spirit speaks to Philip.

cards.question: The Spirit tells Philip to leave the official's chariot alone and keep walking south.

cards.text: So Philip RUNS up to that chariot, close enough to hear the man reading Isaiah. Running beside a chariot? I hop across my own bakery on this gold base and need to sit down.

cards.question: Philip hears the Ethiopian official reading Isaiah. What does Philip ask him?

answers.text: Do you understand what you are reading
Where did you get that scroll
Why are you reading it out here

cards.question: The Ethiopian official tells Philip he understands Isaiah just fine on his own.

cards.text: He asks how he could understand unless someone guides him, and he invites Philip up to sit with him. I spent years in a junk drawer next to instruction manuals and never understood a single one, so I respect a man who asks for help.

Here's what he's reading: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.” It goes on to say He was deprived of justice, and His life was removed from the earth.

cards.question: The Ethiopian official has a question about this Scripture from Isaiah. What does he want to know?

answers.text: Whether the prophet means himself or someone else
Whether the prophet wrote it while in Jerusalem
Whether the lamb in it was ever found again

cards.question: Philip begins with that very Scripture and tells the official the good news about ___.
As they travel along and come to some water, the official asks what is there to prevent him from being baptized.
The official orders the chariot to stop, and Philip baptizes him right there in the water.

cards.text: They come up out of the water, and the Spirit of the Lord carries Philip away. One second he's standing there dripping, and the next second the official sees him no more.

cards.question: With Philip gone, the newly baptized official goes on his way ___.
Philip turns up at Azotus. What does he do from there?

answers.text: Preaches the gospel in every town to Caesarea
Heads straight back to the apostles in Jerusalem
Rests in Azotus until the angel comes back

findings.problem: The instruction-manual joke ends with a tag that explains it: 'so I respect a man who asks for help.' That line spells out how the punchline connects to the official asking for a guide. It also flattens the joke into a nice-dad remark. Cut the tag and let 'never understood a single one' land on its own, or push the line further.

The wrong answer 'Whether the lamb in it was ever found again' takes the sheep-and-lamb picture as if it were a real lost animal. It reads as silly next to the other two answers, which are serious questions a reader of Isaiah might ask. Replace it with a believable question about the prophet or the text.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
